name: Murasaki Shikibu
shortBio: Heian Japanese novelist, Buddhist thinker, and aesthetic theorist whose The Tale of Genji articulated mono no aware (the pathos of impermanent things) as a profound ethical and phenomenological sensibility.
centralQuestion: How does sensitive attunement to Buddhist impermanence (mujo) generate ethical empathy (mono no aware) and self-knowledge across human desire and loss?

keyWorks.title: The Tale of Genji (Genji Monogatari)
keyWorks.description: Monumental philosophical narrative exploring karma, emotional resonance, and aesthetic awareness in Heian court society, including its defense of fiction as truth.

keyWorks.title: The Diary of Lady Murasaki
keyWorks.description: Reflective journal examining female court subjectivity, literary judgment, and philosophical critique of contemporaries.
